deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three unrelated items.

(A) Top: a differential formula from orbit theory.
 d(Loc.C.M) = [first term crossed out, apparently d lgv] − p/(p−p') · d lgv/(1+e cos(lgv − a_p))^2 − p'/(p−p') · d lgv/(1+e' cos(lgv − a_p'))^2.
- Here lgv is presumably a longitude-type angle θ. Each term dθ/(1+e cos(θ−ω))^2 is, up to the factor p^(3/2)/√μ, the time element dt = r^2 dθ/√(μp) of a conic r = p/(1+e cos(θ−ω)).
- The formula therefore combines the time/mean-motion elements of two conics with parameters p, p', eccentricities e, e' and apsidal longitudes a_p, a_p'. The weights are p/(p−p') and p'/(p−p').
- The meaning of 'Loc. C. M.' and the exact signs cannot be fixed from this page. Nothing on the page is derived from the formula.

(B) Middle: a table of quadrature coefficients.
- Row m (m = 1..7) carries a prefactor (1/m!)·c_m: 1·1/2, 1/2·1/6, 1/6·1/4, 1/24·1/30, 1/120·1/12, 1/720·1/84, 1/5040·1/24. These products give the common denominators D_m = 2, 12, 24, 720, 1440, 60480, 120960.
- Each row then lists numerators N_{m,j} (my identification) with I(m,j) = ∫_0^1 binomial(t+j, m) dt = N_{m,j}/D_m, for j = m−1, m−2, …, 0.
- So row m gives the coefficient of the m-th difference in ∫ f over one interval [x_0, x_0+h]. This holds when f is expanded by Newton's formula from a difference taken at any of the possible positions in the difference table. The rows are:
 - m=1: 1/2
 - m=2: 5, −1 (/12)
 - m=3: 9, −1, 1 (/24)
 - m=4: 251, −19, 11, −19 (/720)
 - m=5: 475, −27, 11, −11, 27 (/1440)
 - m=6: 19087, −863, 271, −191, 271, −863 (/60480)
 - m=7: 36799, −1375, 351, −191, 191, −351, 1375 (/120960)
- The columns have recognisable meanings:
 - j = m−1 (first entry): the Adams–Bashforth backward-difference coefficients γ_m = 1/2, 5/12, 3/8, 251/720, 95/288, 19087/60480, 5257/17280.
 - j = 0 (last entry): Gregory's coefficients, which are also the Adams–Moulton γ*_m: 1/2, −1/12, 1/24, −19/720, 3/160, −863/60480, 275/24192.
 - Middle entries: the central (Gauss–Encke) coefficients −1/12, 11/720, −191/60480, and for odd m their halves ±1/24, ±11/1440, ±191/120960.
- The table is evidently built with the recursion I(m,j) − I(m,j−1) = I(m−1,j−1) and the symmetry I(m,j) = (−1)^m I(m, m−2−j).
- This explains the correction in row 7. Gauss first wrote 20412, −1375, 462 … −462. The value 462 = 11·42 is I(5,2) rescaled to /60480, an intermediate of row 6. He then replaced these with 36799, 351, and added '351 + 1375' at the end of the row.

(C) Small numbers '4 / 8 / 232 8' at the right margin: unexplained scratch.

(D) Lower table, an analogous attempt with different denominators.
- Rows: 1·1/2: +1; 2·(1/2·1/6): +4 +4; 3·(1/6·1/12): +19 +13 −5; 4·(1/24·1/60): +337 +157 …
- The denominators are 2, 12, 72, 1440. The table is incomplete.
- I could not identify the integral it represents. It does not obey the same difference recursion as table (B). It may be a second-sum (double-integration) or other-interval variant, or an abandoned trial.
errors: Row 7 of table (B) was first computed wrongly (20412 … +462 … −462); Gauss himself corrected it to 36799, −1375, 351, −191, 191, −351, 1375, which is correct.
All final entries of table (B) check out against ∫_0^1 binomial(t+j,m) dt.

Table (D) cannot be verified because its intended quantity is unidentified. The equal entries 4/12, 4/12 do not satisfy the difference recursion valid for (B), so it may contain errors or be a different construction.
In formula (A) both correction terms carry a minus sign and the weights are p/(p−p') and p'/(p−p'). Without context it is unclear whether this sign pattern is intended.

results.what: Complete table of coefficients ∫_0^1 C(t+j,m) dt (m ≤ 7, all j) for integrating Newton's interpolation series over one step, with differences taken at any position in the table.
results.modern_name: Coefficients of linear multistep / mechanical quadrature formulas: Adams–Bashforth γ_m, Adams–Moulton/Gregory γ*_m, and Gauss–Encke central coefficients
results.usually_credited_to: Gregory (1670) for the j=0 column; Adams (1855, published by Bashforth 1883) for the Adams–Bashforth column; Gauss/Encke (Encke 1837, 'Über mechanische Quadratur') for the central coefficients

results.what: Recursion I(m,j) − I(m,j−1) = I(m−1,j−1) and symmetry I(m,j) = (−1)^m I(m,m−2−j) used to fill the table
results.modern_name: Pascal-type recursion for integrated binomial coefficients

results.what: Time element of two conics in terms of the true-longitude-type angle, dθ/(1+e cos(θ−ω))^2, combined with weights p/(p−p'), p'/(p−p')

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's work on mechanical quadrature with difference tables (transmitted through Encke 1837) is well known. The central and Gregory columns are therefore expected. A clean table that also contains the Adams–Bashforth column (251/720, 95/288, 19087/60480, 5257/17280) in Gauss's hand, before Adams' 1855 work, is a nice confirmation of priority. It is not a major new attribution, since such coefficients follow directly from integrating Newton's formula.

checkable.asserts: First column (j=m−1) gives the Adams–Bashforth coefficients listed by Gauss.
Last column (j=0) gives Gregory / Adams–Moulton coefficients.
Corrected row m=7 of the table.
Gauss's row prefactors (1/m!)·c_m equal the common denominators of the rows.
